Compartment 4.13.0 is a compatibility release: it is about Compartment installing, starting and staying connected on every system and in every agent, including the places it used to fail quietly - agents' sandboxed shells, Windows on ARM, Intel Macs, containers, and GUI apps that cannot see your PATH. 4.12.0 was merged but never published, so its 79 stability fixes ship here too.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `Compartment-4.13.0.pkg` | macOS on Apple silicon, one click, with the menu bar app |
| `Compartment-4.13.0.dmg` | macOS on Apple silicon, drag to Applications |
| `Compartment-4.13.0-intel.pkg` | **new:** macOS on Intel, one click |
| `Compartment-4.13.0-intel.dmg` | **new:** macOS on Intel, drag to Applications |
| `compartment-4.13.0.mcpb` | **new:** Claude Desktop extension (attached a few minutes after publishing) |
| `compartment-4.13.0-py3-none-any.whl` | pip and offline installs, any OS |
| `compartment-4.13.0.tar.gz` | source |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | checksums of all of the above |

Everything here was built from this tag on GitHub's machines, and PyPI carries the very same wheel and sdist.

```bash
pipx install compartment && compartment init      # or: uv tool install compartment
```

The Mac app needs macOS 13.4 or newer. The README's new **Where it runs** table gives every system, CPU and Python version CI tests.

## Highlights

- **Works from an agent's own shell.** Claude Code and Codex run commands in a sandbox that blocks the macOS boot clock, Unix sockets and some file modes. Every `compartment` command an agent ran there used to fail with "Cannot identify this boot session". It now uses the vault you unlocked, embeds in-process, and never hangs.
- **Clients can always start the server.** `compartment integrate` writes the full path of the installed command. GUI apps started from the Dock or Start menu do not inherit your PATH, and a bare `compartment` failed there with "spawn compartment ENOENT".
- **`pip install compartment` works on Windows on ARM and Intel Macs again.** Two indirect dependencies (cryptography, argon2-cffi-bindings) stopped shipping wheels there, and pip tried to compile them. A new CI check fails if any supported platform would need a compiler again.
- **Intel Mac installer.** The Mac app is built for Apple silicon and Intel, and no longer bundles libraries that need a newer macOS than it says it supports.
- **A plugin in every store.**
  - New: a Claude Desktop extension (`.mcpb`).
  - Updated: the Claude Code plugin now carries a version, plus better Codex and MCP Registry listings, and corrected Gemini CLI and LM Studio listings.
  - Ready to submit: Docker MCP Catalog and Continue entries.
  - The full list is in the new `docs/PLUGINS.md`.

## Agents and clients

- 33 clients, adding Kiro, Amazon Q Developer CLI, Junie, Factory and Crush. Continue gets its own block file, and Goose gets a real YAML extension entry.
- **New config locations:** Claude Desktop's Microsoft Store build, Cline 4, Kilo Code 7, Cline/Roo/Kilo inside Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium and Flathub VS Code, and Zed on macOS.
- **Moved config homes followed:** `CODEX_HOME`, `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, `QWEN_HOME`, `COPILOT_HOME`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and OpenClaw's state and config variables.
- **OpenClaw:** the server is written under `mcp.servers`, where current OpenClaw reads it. An old entry is moved there.
- **Config edits keep what is already there:**
  - Comments in Zed and VS Code files, and the user's own keys in a Codex entry.
  - Each file's own line endings.
  - Files saved by Notepad or PowerShell (byte order mark, UTF-16) are read correctly.
  - `integrate codex` can no longer corrupt config.toml.
- **Claude Code capture hook:** quoted correctly for Git Bash on Windows and non-ASCII user names. It also follows `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `autoMemoryDirectory`.
- **MCP:**
  - Every tool says it never reaches the internet.
  - Tool errors reach the model with their reason.
  - A missing vault says "run `compartment init`" instead of "locked".
  - `compartment serve --vault PATH` works.
  - Closing a client's terminal keeps the session's audit rows.
  - mcp 1.x no longer logs a stderr line per request.
  - The real floor is mcp 1.21.2: nothing older runs beside today's pydantic.

## Operating systems

- **Windows:**
  - A machine up for more than 24.9 days no longer relocks the vault and deletes the unlock credential.
  - A process started without USERNAME no longer deletes everyone's credential.
  - No console windows behind the tray or the panel's buttons, and start at sign-in uses pythonw.
  - With fast user switching, another user's tray is not taken for yours.
  - Saves outlast OneDrive and antivirus holding the vault.
  - The lock always takes byte zero.
  - The Visual C++ message names the ARM64 installer on ARM.
- **macOS:**
  - An acknowledged store survives a power cut (F_FULLFSYNC).
  - The boot time is read in-process instead of forking `sysctl` on every vault open.
- **Linux:**
  - Start at login keeps working on Xfce, MATE, Cinnamon and LXQt.
  - It is refused, with a reason, inside Flatpak or a strict Snap.
  - A missing Tk names the exact package for your distribution.
  - `compartment dash` works on WSL (it opens the Windows browser) and on headless machines (it prints how to reach it).
- **Containers:**
  - A container run as an arbitrary user with no home folder works, with `COMPARTMENT_PASSPHRASE` or `COMPARTMENT_SESSION_DIR`.
  - Inference threads respect CPU quotas.
  - The Docker image reads a host user's vault, runs with `--network none` and keeps the offline guard on.
- **BSD, Alpine, Termux:**
  - FreeBSD, NetBSD, DragonFly and OpenBSD get the boot clock.
  - OpenBSD's on-disk shared memory is refused for the unlock secret.
  - The installers point Alpine, FreeBSD and Termux at their own onnxruntime package.
- **Installers:**
  - They handle "externally-managed-environment" Pythons (Debian 12+, Ubuntu 23.04+, Fedora, Arch, Homebrew).
  - They pick a Python that works on the machine.
  - They survive being re-run or piped into a shell.
- **Offline guard:** it now refuses every socket family that can reach another machine, not just IP: Bluetooth, VSOCK/Hyper-V (WSL 2's host) and packet sockets.

## Storage

- A disk that fills up or a sync that fails part way through a store no longer leaves a vault that will not open.
- Text containing half an emoji (a lone surrogate) is stored and searched instead of failing.
- Imports with odd dates, NaN, or Unicode line separators no longer break search.
- A save by another process is noticed even on filesystems with coarse timestamps.
- A store whose journal write failed is never treated as written.
- A vault on a filesystem that cannot lock says so at once.
- Above 20,000 records the exact index stays when usearch has no SIMD (as inside a sandbox). Rebuilding HNSW there took 50 s at 25,000 records on every open.
- A Python whose SQLite lacks FTS5 gets a clear message.
- `COMPARTMENT_PASSPHRASE` is still tried when the boot-session lookup fails.

## For maintainers

- **Release workflow:** a tag now builds every download, Intel included, and drafts the release. Publishing it uploads those same files to PyPI, then builds and attaches the Claude Desktop extension.
- **CI coverage:**
  - Every declared Python (3.11-3.14) on Windows, macOS and Linux, plus ARM64 Linux, Windows on ARM and an Intel Mac.
  - The macOS app on both architectures.
  - The built wheel installed with pipx and driven over MCP on each system.
  - The suite at the lowest dependency versions the bounds allow.
  - A weekly wheel-coverage check.
- **Failure reports:** a red job states its failing tests on the run page.
- **One-time store submissions** that need an account: listed in `docs/PLUGINS.md`.
